doc.title: Howie Shear interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2014

chapter: Jazz as a career and wrap-up
title: Current work and the future for young musicians
summary: Little studio work lately; he teaches and tells students to create their own niche.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well I’ve enjoyed this conversation a lot.
What’s in the near future for you? Anything —

Well I go back, I teach, like I said, at several schools. And no studio things coming up but they just pop up at the last minute anyway. Because it’s not like it used to be where they said I’m going to fill these chairs two weeks in advance. Because now there are so many people that are out of work, musicians that they could call — if I can’t make it they’ll make another call and they’ll make another call and they’ll make another call.
God, where are all these graduates, these jazz graduates going?

I know yeah. There’s not enough music being written for live musicians anymore. So what are they going to do as players or teachers? There are many musicians, since my doctorate I haven’t been interviewed for one teaching job even though I have several universities, they just know me as a player and a writer out there so they think of me for that. And they know I have a doctorate. But I didn’t get these jobs I have because I have a doctorate. Because there are no full time jobs around now. Teachers who are teaching a lot of them wouldn’t even be teaching. They’re just musicians who never thought they’d be teaching but they happen to fall into it and they won’t leave because there’s not

enough playing work so — exactly. So there’s not a lot of work for teachers, players, composers and orchestrators. It’s a very difficult life right now. I sort of made a name in town for myself early on when there was a lot of work. And then once they hear you play well you’re sort of in. But now these newer guys can’t even get heard because there’s no work. And if there is work they call the players like myself who have been in town for 25, 30 years. It’s very difficult but that’s the age old question right now, where are these students — and I talk to my students about that too. I said figure out what it is, you know, create your own niche. You have to create your own niche because there might not be one opened up for a long time. So if there’s something that you do well that might not exist at this point, pursue that. It might open up the rest of your life for you to be able to earn a living.
